name: Playwright Tests
on:
    push:
        branches: [main]
    pull_request:
        branches: [main]
    workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
    test:
        timeout-minutes: 30
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
            contents: read
            packages: read

        strategy:
            fail-fast: false
            matrix:
                include:
                    - project: chromium
                      browser: chromium
                    - project: firefox
                      browser: firefox
                    - project: webkit
                      browser: webkit
                    - project: mobile
                      browser: chromium
                    - project: tablet
                      browser: chromium

        env:
            # Hardcoded CI-only values — none of these are production secrets.
            DATABASE_PASSWORD: ci_test_password
            DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD: ci_test_app_password
            # Used only by the "Push Prisma schema" step below (DDL). The app
            # under test, and the seed step it triggers, run on the
            # non-privileged footy_app user via DATABASE_URL (SYS-444) - that
            # user is baked into the seeded DB image (see
            # publish-seeded-db-image.yml).
            MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
            DATABASE_URL: REDACTED

            # Any non-empty string works for Better Auth in tests (used for
            # signing tokens; tests bypass auth via mock cookies).
            BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: ci-better-auth-secret-for-playwright-tests-only

            # Dummy OAuth credentials — tests use cookie-based mock auth and
            # never trigger a real OAuth flow.
            AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: dummy-google-client-id
            AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: dummy-google-client-secret
            AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID: dummy-microsoft-client-id
            AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET: dummy-microsoft-client-secret

            # Sentry source-map upload is disabled when SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN is
            # absent (see next.config.mjs disableSourceMapUpload). No token
            # needed here.

            # Pulled by docker-compose.ci.yml in place of a bare mariadb:lts,
            # pre-loaded with schema + seed data by
            # publish-seeded-db-image.yml. `prisma db push` below still runs
            # regardless, as a cheap safety net for branches whose schema
            # changes haven't been baked into this image yet - see the "Push
            # Prisma schema" step for what happens when that image is stale
            # enough to need it.
            SEEDED_DB_IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/next-www-toastboy-db-test-seeded:latest

        steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v7
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
              with:
                  node-version: 24
            - name: Install dependencies
              run: npm ci
            - name: Log in to GHCR
              uses: docker/login-action@v4.6.0
              with:
                  registry: ghcr.io
                  username: ${{ github.actor }}
                  password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
            - name: Start docker stack (database, mailpit, etc.)
              run: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.ci.yml up -d
            - name: Wait for database
              run: |
                  for i in {1..30}; do
                    if [ "$(docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' $(docker compose ps -q db))" = "healthy" ]; then
                      exit 0
                    fi
                    sleep 2
                  done
                  docker compose logs db
                  exit 1
            - name: Push Prisma schema
              id: schema_push
              run: |
                  # Try a plain push first: when the pre-seeded image already
                  # matches prisma/schema.prisma (the common case), this is a
                  # no-op and the image's baked-in seed data is still valid,
                  # so Playwright can use the SKIP_DB_SEED fast path below. On
                  # a branch whose schema has diverged from the last-published
                  # image (e.g. a column rename/drop with real data still in
                  # it, like this repo's PlayerRecord/GameDay/Outcome
                  # changes), Prisma refuses without --accept-data-loss - in
                  # that case, reapply with the flag and mark that the baked
                  # seed data no longer matches the new schema and must be
                  # regenerated from scratch.
                  set +e
                  npx prisma db push
                  status=$?
                  set -e
                  if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then
                    echo "reseed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  else
                    echo "Pre-seeded image schema has diverged - reapplying with --accept-data-loss and forcing a full reseed."
                    npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss
                    echo "reseed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  fi
            - name: Build Next.js app
              run: npm run build
            - name: Install Playwright Browser (${{ matrix.browser }})
              run: npx playwright install --with-deps ${{ matrix.browser }}
            - name: Run Playwright tests (${{ matrix.project }})
              env:
                  # Enables cookie-based mock auth in the production-built server
                  # (see src/lib/auth.server.ts isMockAuthEnabled).
                  PLAYWRIGHT_TEST: "true"
                  # The db container above already has seed data baked in -
                  # unless the schema push just had to reconcile it (see the
                  # "Push Prisma schema" step), in which case that data no
                  # longer matches the current schema and a full reseed is
                  # required.
                  SKIP_DB_SEED: ${{ steps.schema_push.outputs.reseed != 'true' && 'true' || '' }}
              run: npx playwright test --project=${{ matrix.project }}
            - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
              if: always()
              with:
                  name: playwright-report-${{ matrix.project }}
                  path: playwright-report/
                  retention-days: 30

        runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        steps:
            - name: Checkout code
              uses: actions/checkout@v7

              uses: actions/setup-node@v7

            - name: Install dependencies

            - name: Generate prisma client and zod schemas
              run: npm run generate

            - name: Run tests

            - name: Upload results to Codecov
              uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7

=== ci compose ===
# CI override for docker-compose.yml: replaces the bare `db` image with one
# pre-loaded with the current schema and seed data (built by
# .github/workflows/publish-seeded-db-image.yml), so Playwright matrix jobs
# don't each have to regenerate the same fixture data from scratch. Not used
# locally - local dev needs the plain mariadb:lts image so `npm run migrate`
# and schema iteration work normally.
#
# Usage: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.ci.yml up -d
services:
  db:
    image: ${SEEDED_DB_IMAGE}
    # The base file mounts a named volume over /var/lib/mysql for durability
    # across `docker compose down`/`up` on a dev machine. In CI that would
    # shadow the data already baked into the image with an empty volume on
    # every fresh runner, silently discarding the seed - so it must be
    # dropped here, not just left empty (Compose merges list fields across
    # files by default; `!reset` is required to actually remove one).
    volumes: !reset []

name: Storybook Tests

on:
    push:
        branches: [main]
    pull_request:

jobs:
    test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
            contents: read
            pull-requests: write
            checks: write

        steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v7

            - name: Setup Node
              uses: actions/setup-node@v7
              with:
                  node-version: 24
                  cache: npm

            # So Chromatic doesn't get confused
            - name: Configure git identity
              run: |
                  git config --global user.email "ci@github.com"
                  git config --global user.name "GitHub Actions"

            - name: Install dependencies
              run: npm ci

            - name: Generate prisma client and zod schemas
              run: npm run generate

            - name: Build Storybook
              run: npm run build:storybook

            - name: Start Storybook
              run: |
                  npm run storybook -- --ci --disable-telemetry --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6006 > /tmp/storybook.log 2>&1 &
                  npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006

            - name: Run Storybook tests
              run: npm run test:storybook

            - name: Upload Storybook logs
              if: always()
              uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
              with:
                  name: storybook-test-logs
                  path: /tmp/storybook.log
                  if-no-files-found: ignore
                  retention-days: 14

64:CI workflows are structured so that **PR-triggered workflows never access 1Password**. Only workflows that run on `push: main` (deploy, Terraform apply) load secrets via the 1Password service account. This limits the blast radius of a supply-chain attack: a compromised npm package running in a PR test suite cannot exfiltrate production credentials.
81:Dependabot PRs are automatically merged once all required status checks pass, using GitHub's native auto-merge feature ([`.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`](.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml)). The workflow only enables the auto-merge flag — no code is checked out or run. For this to work:
88:As a defence against supply-chain attacks (where a malicious version is published and quickly flagged by the community), auto-merge is withheld for any npm package whose new version was published less than **7 days ago**. The workflow queries the npm registry for the publish timestamp of each updated package and posts a comment on the PR if any package is too new, listing which ones and how old they are. The check re-runs on each push; once all packages have aged past the threshold, auto-merge is enabled automatically without further intervention.
92:The threshold is controlled by `MIN_AGE_DAYS` at the top of the age-check step in [`.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`](.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml).

81:Dependabot PRs are automatically merged once all required status checks pass, using GitHub's native auto-merge feature ([`.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`](.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml)). # Next.js + MySQL rewrite of <www.toastboy.co.uk>

This project is based on [Azure + MySQL example code](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/vercel-nextjs-app-azure-db-mysql) from [Prisma](https://www.prisma.io/) using [Mantine Components](https://mantine.dev/), [Tabler Icons](https://tabler-icons-react.vercel.app/) and [Better Auth](https://better-auth.vercel.app/). It uses [Sentry](https://sentry.io/) for app monitoring, [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) for unit testing and [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) for end-to-end testing. Test coverage is uploaded to [Codecov](https://about.codecov.io/) and [ESLint](https://www.npmjs.com/package/eslint) results are monitored in GitHub Actions using [Reviewdog](https://github.com/reviewdog/reviewdog).

[![CodeQL](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/github-code-scanning/codeql/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/github-code-scanning/codeql)
[![Unit Tests with Coverage](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/unit-tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/unit-tests.yml)
[![Playwright Tests](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/playwright.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/playwright.yml)
[![Storybook Tests](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/storybook.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/storybook.yml)
[![Chromatic](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/chromatic.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/chromatic.yml)
[![Reviewdog](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/lint.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/lint.yml)
[![Knip](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/knip.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/knip.yml)
[![Terraform](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/terraform.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/toastboy/next-www-toastboy/actions/workflows/terraform.yml)

## Azure App Registrations

Three Azure AD app registrations are managed by Terraform in [`terraform/main.tf`](terraform/main.tf), each scoped to the minimum permissions needed:

| App         | Display Name                | Purpose                                 | Permissions                                          |
| ----------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| **Auth**    | Next www toastboy – Auth    | Microsoft social login via Better Auth  | Delegated: `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `User.Read` |
| **Storage** | Next www toastboy – Storage | Azure Blob Storage access via RBAC      | None (RBAC role assignment only)                     |
| **Mail**    | Next www toastboy – Mail    | Transactional email via Microsoft Graph | Application: `Mail.Send` (admin-consented)           |

Terraform outputs the client IDs and secrets for each registration, which are synced to 1Password (vault `next-www-toastboy`) by the [Terraform workflow](.github/workflows/terraform.yml) after each apply. The env var mapping is:

| App     | Client ID env var          | Client secret env var          |
| ------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Auth    | `AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID` | `AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` |
| Storage | `STORAGE_CLIENT_ID`        | `STORAGE_CLIENT_SECRET`        |
| Mail    | `MAIL_GRAPH_CLIENT_ID`     | `MAIL_GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET`     |

### Running Terraform locally

To validate a change (e.g. a provider version bump) before pushing:

```shell
terraform login   # one-off; opens a browser, stores a personal API token in ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json
cd terraform
op run --env-file ./.env -- terraform init
terraform validate
op run --env-file ./.env -- terraform plan
```

The `cloud` block in [`providers.tf`](terraform/providers.tf) points at Terraform Cloud (org `toastboy`, workspace `next-www-toastboy`), which holds state and runs `plan`/`apply` remotely — the local CLI just streams the output. `terraform login` is only needed once per machine; CI uses a separate service token (`TF_API_TOKEN`) so there's nothing to share or configure for that.

`terraform apply` is only ever run from CI on push to `main` (see [GitHub Actions Secrets](#github-actions-secrets)) — use `plan` locally to check a change, then let CI apply it once merged.

## Secrets

All secrets should be managed by 1Password, in the exclusive vault "next-www-toastboy" and referenced from the `.env` file. This file is safe to commit to source control since it only contains references, not values. Preface all commands which might need secret values in the environment with the op cli, like this:

```shell
op run --env-file ./.env -- npm run build
```

The `importlivedb` script needs two env files:

```shell
op run --env-file src/lib/importlivedb/.env --env-file ./.env -- npm run importlivedb
```

## GitHub Actions Secrets

CI workflows are structured so that **PR-triggered workflows never access 1Password**. Only workflows that run on `push: main` (deploy, Terraform apply) load secrets via the 1Password service account. This limits the blast radius of a supply-chain attack: a compromised npm package running in a PR test suite cannot exfiltrate production credentials.

The split between secret stores reflects this:

| Secret                     | Store                               | Used by                                                                          |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` | GitHub Actions secret               | Terraform apply and 1Password sync (main only)                                   |

## Running Playwright Tests Locally (macOS)

The `stdbuf` command used in some Linux CI seed scripts is not available on macOS by default. The `seed:playwright` and `seed:ci` scripts in `package.json` do not use `stdbuf`, so they work on both platforms.

Before running Playwright tests for the first time — or after any Prisma schema change — initialise the dedicated test database:

```shell
npm run setup:playwright
```

This creates the `footy` test database (via `prisma db push`) and regenerates the Prisma client. You only need to repeat it when the schema changes.

Then run all E2E tests:

```shell
npx playwright test
```

The test runner starts a local Next.js server automatically, seeds the test database, and tears everything down when done.

## Sentry Sampling and Quota Controls

The Sentry setup in this project now uses conservative defaults designed to fit
the free tier and avoid noisy events. You can override sampling behaviour with
environment variables when needed.

name: Link Check

on:
    push:
        branches: [main]
    pull_request:
    workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
    link-check:
        name: Broken link check (public surface)
        timeout-minutes: 20
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
            contents: read
            packages: read

        env:
            # Hardcoded CI-only values — none of these are production secrets.
            # Kept byte-for-byte in step with playwright.yml: this job stands up
            # the same docker stack against the same pre-seeded DB image.
            DATABASE_PASSWORD: ci_test_password
            DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD: ci_test_app_password
            MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
            DATABASE_URL: REDACTED

            BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: ci-better-auth-secret-for-link-check-only

            AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: dummy-google-client-id
            AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: dummy-google-client-secret
            AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID: dummy-microsoft-client-id
            AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET: dummy-microsoft-client-secret

            SEEDED_DB_IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/next-www-toastboy-db-test-seeded:latest

        steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v7
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
              with:
                  node-version: 24
                  cache: "npm"
            - name: Install dependencies
              run: npm ci
            - name: Log in to GHCR
              uses: docker/login-action@v4.6.0
              with:
                  registry: ghcr.io
                  username: ${{ github.actor }}
                  password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
            - name: Start docker stack (database, mailpit, etc.)
              run: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.ci.yml up -d
            - name: Wait for database
              run: |
                  for i in {1..30}; do
                    if [ "$(docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' $(docker compose ps -q db))" = "healthy" ]; then
                      exit 0
                    fi
                    sleep 2
                  done
                  docker compose logs db
                  exit 1
            - name: Push Prisma schema
              id: schema_push
              run: |
                  # Same recipe as playwright.yml: a plain push is a no-op when
                  # the pre-seeded image already matches prisma/schema.prisma
                  # (the common case) and the baked-in seed data stays valid. On
                  # a branch whose schema has diverged, Prisma refuses without
                  # --accept-data-loss — reapply with the flag and force a full
                  # reseed so the data matches the new schema.
                  set +e
                  npx prisma db push
                  status=$?
                  set -e
                  if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then
                    echo "reseed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  else
                    echo "Pre-seeded image schema has diverged - reapplying with --accept-data-loss and forcing a full reseed."
                    npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss
                    echo "reseed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  fi
            - name: Seed database
              run: |
                  # Mirrors e2e/global-setup.ts: the pre-seeded image already
                  # carries the fixture data, so normally we only re-point the
                  # single "upcoming" game day at the next Friday. A full reseed
                  # is needed only when the schema push above had to reconcile a
                  # diverged image.
                  if [ "${{ steps.schema_push.outputs.reseed }}" = "true" ]; then
                    npm run seed:ci
                  else
                    npm run refresh:upcoming-gameday:ci
                  fi
            - name: Build Next.js app
              run: npm run build
            - name: Start production server
              run: |
                  npm run start:ci > /tmp/next-start.log 2>&1 &
                  npx wait-on --timeout 120000 http://127.0.0.1:3000
            - name: Check links
              run: npx linkinator http://127.0.0.1:3000 --config linkinator.config.json --format json > linkinator-report.json
            - name: Upload linkinator report
              if: always()
              uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
              with:
                  name: linkinator-report
                  path: linkinator-report.json
                  retention-days: 30
            - name: Upload server log
              if: always()
              uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
              with:
                  name: next-start-log
                  path: /tmp/next-start.log
                  if-no-files-found: ignore
                  retention-days: 7

        name: Broken link check (public surface)
        timeout-minutes: 20
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
            contents: read
            packages: read

        env:
            # Hardcoded CI-only values — none of these are production secrets.
            # Kept byte-for-byte in step with playwright.yml: this job stands up
            # the same docker stack against the same pre-seeded DB image.
            DATABASE_PASSWORD: ci_test_password
            DATABASE_APP_PASSWORD: ci_test_app_password
            MIGRATE_DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
            DATABASE_URL: REDACTED

            BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: ci-better-auth-secret-for-link-check-only

            AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: dummy-google-client-id
            AUTH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: dummy-google-client-secret
            AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID: dummy-microsoft-client-id
            AUTH_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET: dummy-microsoft-client-secret

            SEEDED_DB_IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/next-www-toastboy-db-test-seeded:latest

        steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v7
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
              with:
                  node-version: 24
                  cache: "npm"
            - name: Install dependencies
              run: npm ci
            - name: Log in to GHCR
              uses: docker/login-action@v4.6.0
              with:
                  registry: ghcr.io
                  username: ${{ github.actor }}
                  password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
            - name: Start docker stack (database, mailpit, etc.)
              run: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.ci.yml up -d
            - name: Wait for database
              run: |
                  for i in {1..30}; do
                    if [ "$(docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' $(docker compose ps -q db))" = "healthy" ]; then
                      exit 0
                    fi
                    sleep 2
                  done
                  docker compose logs db
                  exit 1
            - name: Push Prisma schema
              id: schema_push
              run: |
                  # Same recipe as playwright.yml: a plain push is a no-op when
                  # the pre-seeded image already matches prisma/schema.prisma
                  # (the common case) and the baked-in seed data stays valid. On
                  # a branch whose schema has diverged, Prisma refuses without
                  # --accept-data-loss — reapply with the flag and force a full
                  # reseed so the data matches the new schema.
                  set +e
                  npx prisma db push
                  status=$?
                  set -e
                  if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then
                    echo "reseed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  else
                    echo "Pre-seeded image schema has diverged - reapplying with --accept-data-loss and forcing a full reseed."
                    npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss
                    echo "reseed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  fi
            - name: Seed database
              run: |
                  # Mirrors e2e/global-setup.ts: the pre-seeded image already
                  # carries the fixture data, so normally we only re-point the
                  # single "upcoming" game day at the next Friday. A full reseed
                  # is needed only when the schema push above had to reconcile a
                  # diverged image.
                  if [ "${{ steps.schema_push.outputs.reseed }}" = "true" ]; then
                    npm run seed:ci
                  else
                    npm run refresh:upcoming-gameday:ci
                  fi
            - name: Build Next.js app
              run: npm run build
            - name: Start production server
              run: |
                  npm run start:ci > /tmp/next-start.log 2>&1 &
                  npx wait-on --timeout 120000 http://127.0.0.1:3000
            - name: Check links
              run: npx linkinator http://127.0.0.1:3000 --config linkinator.config.json --format json > linkinator-report.json
            - name: Upload linkinator report
              if: always()
              uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
              with:
                  name: linkinator-report
                  path: linkinator-report.json
                  retention-days: 30
            - name: Upload server log
              if: always()
              uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
              with:
                  name: next-start-log
                  path: /tmp/next-start.log
                  if-no-files-found: ignore
                  retention-days: 7

The test runner starts a local Next.js server automatically, seeds the test database, and tears everything down when done.

## Broken Link Checking

[`.github/workflows/link-check.yml`](.github/workflows/link-check.yml) builds the app, runs it against the seeded CI database, and uses [`linkinator`](https://github.com/JustinBeckwith/linkinator) to recursively crawl the **public** surface from `http://127.0.0.1:3000`. Any non-skipped internal link that returns a 4xx/5xx fails the workflow (and therefore the PR check). The full JSON report is uploaded as a build artifact on every run.

External hosts are deliberately out of scope here so PRs don't break on third-party outages — those are covered by the separate weekly external-link job (SYS-616).

Exclusions live in [`linkinator.config.json`](linkinator.config.json) at the repo root: add a per-URL or per-domain regular expression to the `skip` array to stop a link being checked. The first entry (`^https?://(?!127\.0\.0\.1:3000)`) is what scopes the crawl to internal links; leave it in place and add new exclusions alongside it. The authenticated `src/app/footy/**` admin surface is not yet crawled (it needs the mock-auth cookie and the programmatic API — a follow-up).

To run it locally, start a production build on port 3000 and point the script at it:

```shell
op run --env-file ./.env -- npm run build
npm run start:ci &
npm run linkcheck
```

#!/usr/bin/env node
import process from 'node:process';

const cli = meow(`
	Usage
		$ linkinator LOCATION [ --arguments ]

	Positional arguments

		LOCATION
			Required. Either the URLs or the paths on disk to check for broken links.

	Flags

		--concurrency
			The number of connections to make simultaneously. Defaults to 100.

		--config
			Path to the config file to use. Looks for \`linkinator.config.json\` by default.

		--directory-listing
			Include an automatic directory index file when linking to a directory.
			Defaults to 'false'.

		--clean-urls
			Enable clean URLs (extensionless links). When enabled, links like '/about'
			will automatically resolve to '/about.html' if the file exists.
			Mimics behavior of modern static hosting platforms like Vercel.
			Defaults to 'false'.

		--format, -f
			Return the data in CSV or JSON format.

		--header, -h
			List of additional headers to be include in the request. use key:value notation.

		--help
			Show this command.

		--version
			Show the version number.

		--markdown
			Automatically parse and scan markdown if scanning from a location on disk.

		--recurse, -r
			Recursively follow links on the same root domain.

		--sitemap
			Crawl every page listed in /sitemap.xml. Sitemap indexes are followed recursively.

		--sitemap-url
			Use an explicit sitemap URL. Can be specified multiple times, but cannot be combined with --sitemap.

		--check-css
			Extract and check URLs found in CSS properties (inline styles, <style> tags, and external CSS files).
			This includes url() functions, @import statements, and other CSS URL references.
			Defaults to false.

		--check-fragments
			Validate fragment identifiers (URL anchors like #section-name) exist on the target HTML page.
			Invalid fragments will be marked as broken. Only checks server-rendered HTML (not JavaScript-added fragments).
			Defaults to false.

		--skip-fragment
			List of regular expressions for fragments whose validation should be skipped.
			The underlying URL is still checked. Can be specified multiple times.

		--redirects
			Control how redirects are handled. Options are 'allow' (default, follows redirects),
			'warn' (follows but emits warnings), or 'error' (treats redirects as broken).

		--require-https
			Enforce HTTPS links. Options are 'off' (default, accepts both HTTP and HTTPS),
			'warn' (accepts both but emits warnings for HTTP), or 'error' (treats HTTP links as broken).

		--allow-insecure-certs
			Allow invalid or self-signed SSL certificates. Useful for local development with
			untrusted certificates. Defaults to false.

		--retry,
			Automatically retry requests that return HTTP 429 responses and include
			a 'retry-after' header. Defaults to false.

		--retry-errors,
			Automatically retry requests that return 5xx or unknown response.

		--retry-errors-count,
			How many times should an error be retried?

		--retry-errors-jitter,
			Random jitter applied to error retry.

		--server-root
			When scanning a locally directory, customize the location on disk
			where the server is started.  Defaults to the path passed in [LOCATION].

		--skip, -s
			List of urls in regexy form to not include in the check.
			Can be specified multiple times.

		--status-code
			Control how specific HTTP status codes are handled. Format: "CODE:ACTION"
			where CODE is a numeric status code (e.g., 403) or pattern (e.g., 4xx, 5xx)
			and ACTION is one of: ok (success), warn (success with warning),
			skip (ignore link), or error (force failure).
			Can be specified multiple times. Example: --status-code "403:warn"

		--timeout
			Request timeout in ms.  Defaults to 0 (no timeout).

		--url-rewrite-search
			Pattern to search for in urls.  Must be used with --url-rewrite-replace.

		--url-rewrite-replace
			Expression used to replace search content.  Must be used with --url-rewrite-search.

		--user-agent
			The user agent passed in all HTTP requests. Defaults to 'Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_2) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/79.0.3945.117 Safari/537.36'

		--verbosity
			Override the default verbosity for this command. Available options are
			'debug', 'info', 'warning', 'error', and 'none'.  Defaults to 'warning'.

	Examples
		$ linkinator docs/
		$ linkinator https://www.google.com
		$ linkinator . --recurse
		$ linkinator . --skip www.googleapis.com
		$ linkinator . --skip example.com --skip github.com
		$ linkinator . --format CSV
		$ linkinator https://example.com --recurse --check-fragments --redirects error --require-https error --check-css

            SEEDED_DB_IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/next-www-toastboy-db-test-seeded:latest

        steps:
            - uses: actions/checkout@v7
            - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
              with:
                  node-version: 24
                  cache: "npm"
            - name: Install dependencies
              run: npm ci
            - name: Generate Prisma client and Zod schemas
              run: npm run generate
            - name: Log in to GHCR
              uses: docker/login-action@v4.6.0
              with:
                  registry: ghcr.io
                  username: ${{ github.actor }}
                  password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
            - name: Start docker stack (database, mailpit, etc.)
              run: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.ci.yml up -d

              run: |
                  for i in {1..30}; do
                    if [ "$(docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' $(docker compose ps -q db))" = "healthy" ]; then
                      exit 0
                    fi
                    sleep 2
                  done
                  docker compose logs db
                  exit 1
            - name: Push Prisma schema
              id: schema_push
              run: |
                  # Same recipe as playwright.yml: a plain push is a no-op when
                  # the pre-seeded image already matches prisma/schema.prisma
                  # (the common case) and the baked-in seed data stays valid. On
                  # a branch whose schema has diverged, Prisma refuses without
                  # --accept-data-loss — reapply with the flag and force a full
                  # reseed so the data matches the new schema.

                  # carries the fixture data, so normally we only re-point the
                  # single "upcoming" game day at the next Friday. A full reseed
                  # is needed only when the schema push above had to reconcile a
                  # diverged image.
                  if [ "${{ steps.schema_push.outputs.reseed }}" = "true" ]; then

                    npm run refresh:upcoming-gameday:ci

            - name: Start production server

content.text:
Implemented SYS-572 v1 (public-surface broken-link checking in CI).

**New files**
- `linkinator.config.json` (repo root) — `recurse`, `retry`, `concurrency: 20`, `timeout: 10000`, and `skip: ["^https?://(?!127\\.0\\.0\\.1:3000)"]` which scopes the crawl to internal links only. Kept as pure JSON (not the ticket's jsonc sketch) because linkinator loads it with `JSON.parse` and chokes on comments. Verified the regex skips every external host while leaving `127.0.0.1:3000` links checked.
- `.github/workflows/link-check.yml` — standalone workflow, triggers `push: main` / `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch`. Reuses the `playwright.yml` recipe: GHCR login → `docker compose ... up -d` → wait-for-healthy → `prisma db push` with the `--accept-data-loss` fallback + `reseed` output. Then a `Seed database` step mirroring `e2e/global-setup.ts` (full `seed:ci` only on schema divergence, otherwise `refresh:upcoming-gameday:ci`) → `npm run build` → `npm run start:ci &` + `npx wait-on` → `npx linkinator ... --format json > linkinator-report.json`. linkinator exits non-zero on any non-skipped 4xx/5xx, failing the PR check. Report uploaded `if: always()`; a `failure()`-only step prints the broken links since `--format json` hides them from the log.

**Changed**
- `package.json` — `linkinator@^8.1.0` in devDependencies + a `linkcheck` script (`linkinator http://127.0.0.1:3000 --config linkinator.config.json`). The script means knip sees the binary as used, so no `knip.json` change was needed.
- `package-lock.json` — linkinator dependency tree.
- `README.md` — badge + a "Broken Link Checking" section documenting `linkinator.config.json`'s `skip` array as the exclusion point and how to run it locally.

**Checks:** `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `knip` all exit 0 (the two knip config hints are pre-existing). Smoke-tested linkinator locally: it detects a broken internal link and exits 1.

Not touched — these are explicitly v2 / follow-on in the ticket: the authenticated admin crawl, and deleting `e2e/site-crawl.spec.ts` / `e2e/homepage.links.spec.ts`.

content.text:
That `npm run linkcheck` run didn't test the Next.js app — it crawled a **static file server** that's already bound to port 3000 (VS Code's Live Preview: note `___vscode_livepreview_injected_script`, and that it served `.git/`, `.env`, `node_modules/`, `.entire/tmp/*.json`). `lsof` confirms two listeners on :3000, neither of them `next start`. A static server returns `200` for every path and offers directory listings, so linkinator recursed the entire working tree and "passed".

**CI is not affected by this.** The workflow runs `next start` on a clean runner with nothing else on :3000, and `next start` only serves real routes + `/_next/*` + `public/` assets — no directory listings, no source files — so the crawl there stays scoped to links actually rendered in the app's HTML. The `skip` regex is verified correct (external hosts skipped, `127.0.0.1:3000` checked).

**Cleanup done:**
- Removed the stray `linkcheck.out` (34 MB redirect log from an earlier run).
- Added `linkinator-report.json` and `linkcheck.out` to `.gitignore`.
- Added a README caution that `linkcheck` crawls whatever answers on :3000, so nothing else may be bound there.

To get a real local run: stop the Live Preview server (and any `next dev`), then `npm run build` → `npm run start:ci` → `npm run linkcheck`.

- close the Live Preview tab/panel (it shuts down a few seconds after the last preview closes), or
- click the radio-tower / "Port :3000" item in the status bar → Stop.

**Or from the shell:**
```sh
kill 37044              # just the Live Preview server
# or clear everything on :3000 (also kills the stray next-server):
lsof -ti tcp:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill
```

PR CI never gets those (the security model keeps 1Password out of PR workflows), and there's no Azurite in the docker stack — so **`link-check.yml` as I wrote it will fail on every run**, for a reason that has nothing to do with dead links. `e2e/site-crawl.spec.ts` doesn't catch this because a broken `` doesn't trip a React error boundary. **Options:** 1. **Exclude the mugshot endpoint** — add `"/api/footy/player/\\d+/mugshot$"` (or just `"/api/"`) to `skip` in `linkinator.config.json`, documented in the README. Matches the ticket's "add exclusions to the skip array" model. Cheapest; keeps v1 scoped to real navigational links. 2. **Run Azurite** in the CI compose stack and seed the mugshot container — proper coverage, but real work and out of v1 scope. 3. **Fix the route** to fall back to `manofmystery.jpg` / return 404 instead of 500 when storage is unavailable — arguably a genuine bug, but a behaviour change beyond SYS-572. My recommendation: **option 1** for this ticket (narrow regex, not blanket `/api/`), and raise the 500 as its own ticket for option 3 later. Want me to apply the skip entry and update the README?

content.text:
The representative fix is **option 3 — harden the mugshot route so it degrades instead of 500ing** — because it's the only one that changes what a real visitor sees. Today, whenever a blob is missing or Azure hiccups, every game and player page renders broken avatars *and* logs a 500 to Sentry. The link checker just made that visible at scale (1362 references from `/footy/game/*` alone).

What "improve the real site" looks like at the route level:

- **Valid player ⇒ always an image (200).** Read a placeholder that ships with the repo (there's already `src/tests/mocks/data/mugshot.png`; promote a real one to `src/assets/` or `public/`) and return it whenever Azure can't serve a blob — missing secrets, `download()` throws, blob absent, no stream body. The existing "anonymous player ⇒ manofmystery" branch just points at the local placeholder instead of a blob.
- **404 only for a genuinely unknown/NaN player id** — that's the sole `null` path.
- **Never `captureUnexpectedError` for a routine miss.** Downgrade a blob-not-found to a `debug('footy:api')` line / warning breadcrumb; keep error-level only for "Azure unreachable", which is real but should be a fallback, not a broken page.
- **Cache it.** `buildPngResponse` for this route should set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=…, stale-while-revalidate=…` so 1362 game-page references don't stampede storage and a blip doesn't cascade.
- **Fail loud at deploy, not per-request** for missing `STORAGE_*` secrets — a startup/health assertion, so misconfiguration is caught once rather than as 500s forever.

How it ties back to SYS-572: with the route returning a 200 placeholder even without Azure, the `link-check.yml` job needs **no `skip` entry** and becomes a genuine check — it'll still catch a real regression (route throwing on a valid player, wrong content-type, a broken navigational link). This is really a separate app-bug ticket, though, surfaced by SYS-572 rather than part of it.

I'd suggest: file the mugshot-hardening ticket, and land SYS-572 now with a narrow temporary skip (`/api/footy/player/\d+/mugshot$`) that cites it in a README note, to be removed once the route is fixed. Want me to do that and draft the ticket?

content.text: Your two cases only feel contradictory because "succeed" is being asked to cover two different failures. Split them and the tension goes away: - **Unknown entity** (no such player/club/country row, or non-numeric id) → `404`. Same for all three. - **Storage backend unavailable** (missing creds, network error, Azure 5xx/timeout) → `503` + error-level alert. Same for all three — you can't serve anything and you want to know. - **The specific blob is missing, backend healthy** → this is the only place the endpoints legitimately differ. | | blob missing, backend OK | |---|---| | **Mugshot** | serve `manofmystery.jpg`, `200`, no alert (expected — most players have no photo) | | **Badge / flag** | serve a generic placeholder, `200`, **warning-level alert** ("country XYZ has no flag blob") | That gives you "every badge/flag lookup succeeds" for the user, while the warning still enforces your invariant — a missing flag becomes a tracked data bug to fix, not a silent blank and not a page-breaking error. The alternative (404/500 on a missing badge) contradicts "every lookup should succeed" and dumps a data problem onto the client's ``, so I wouldn't. Implementation-wise that's one small helper — `fetchBlobOrFallback(container, key, { fallbackKey, onFallback })` — with the mugshot route passing a silent `onFallback` and the badge/flag routes passing one that logs a warning. Unknown-entity `404` stays in each route where the DB lookup already happens. **Consequence for SYS-572:** even with this fix, PR CI has no storage creds, so all three image endpoints return `503` there. These are `` assets, not navigational links — so the clean call is to **skip `/api/footy/(player|club|country)/…/(mugshot|badge|flag)` in `linkinator.config.json`** (documented), let the PR job own page-to-page integrity, and let a storage-aware job — the `push: main` run with creds, or SYS-616 — own "do all the assets resolve". Net: two tickets — (1) the route-hardening with the split semantics above, (2) SYS-572 lands now with the image-endpoint skip and a note pointing at (1). Want me to draft both?

input.description: ## Problem The three Azure-blob-backed image routes throw and return HTTP 500 whenever blob storage is unavailable or misconfigured, and their "specific blob missing" behaviour is inconsistent: | Route | Blob missing (backend healthy) | Backend unavailable | Unknown entity | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `GET /api/footy/player/[id]/mugshot` | falls back to `manofmystery.jpg` in the same container — but 500s if *that* is missing | 500 | `null` → 404 only for a NaN id or a player row that doesn't exist | | `GET /api/footy/club/[id]/badge` | `null` → 404 | 500 | no entity check — a bad id is indistinguishable from a missing blob (both 404) | | `GET /api/footy/country/[fifaCode]/flag` | `null` → 404 | 500 | no entity check | Consequences on the live site: * Every `` pointing at one of these (player lists, game pages, `FamilyTree`, `PlayerCountryMap`, `DrinkersForm`, `MoneyForm`, `UserButton`, `GameInvitationResponseForm`, …) shows a broken image on any transient Azure blip, and each request logs an error-level event via `captureUnexpectedError` in `handleGET`. * SYS-572's link-check crawl of a full-data instance reported **1442 broken links, every one of them `/api/footy/player/{id}/mugshot` → 500**, because PR CI has no storage credentials (by design — PR workflows never touch 1Password). The endpoints are currently excluded in `linkinator.config.json` via `/api/footy/.+/(?:mugshot|badge|flag)$` pending this fix. ## Decision — split the three failure modes 1. **Unknown / invalid entity** (non-numeric id, no player / club / country row) → **404**. Add the missing entity-existence checks to the badge and flag routes so "no such club" is distinguishable from "club exists, badge blob missing". 2. **Storage backend unavailable** (missing creds, network error, Azure 5xx / timeout) → **503** + error-level capture. Same for all three: nothing can be served and it must be loud. 3. **Specific blob missing, backend healthy** — differs by resource contract: * **Mugshot** (`blob-or-default` contract; most players have no photo): serve the fallback placeholder, **200**, no alert (debug log only). * **Badge / flag** (`blob-always` contract; every valid club / country ought to have one): serve a generic placeholder, **200**, **warning-level alert** naming the club id / FIFA code, so the missing data gets fixed without breaking the page or spamming error-level events. Ship a bundled last-resort placeholder **inside the app** (e.g. `src/assets/…`) for each resource so the response never depends on a second blob fetch succeeding. `manofmystery.jpg` in the mugshots container stays the preferred mugshot fallback; the bundled asset is the final resort when even that can't be fetched. Factor the shared path into one helper, e.g. `fetchBlobOrFallback(container, key, { fallbackKey?, bundledFallback, onFallback })`, with each route supplying its own entity check and `onFallback` (silent for mugshot, `log.warn` for badge / flag). ## Acceptance criteria * [ ] `GET /api/footy/club/[id]/badge` and `.../country/[fifaCode]/flag` return 404 for an unknown club / country, distinct from a missing blob. * [ ] All three routes return a 200 image (real or placeholder) whenever the entity is valid and the storage backend is reachable — including when the specific blob is absent. * [ ] Storage-backend failure returns **503** (not 500) and is captured at error level. * [ ] A missing badge / flag blob for a valid entity emits a warning-level event identifying the entity; a missing mugshot blob does not. * [ ] A bundled in-repo placeholder exists for each resource and is served when no blob (including the container-level fallback) is available. * [ ] Route unit tests cover: unknown entity → 404; blob present → 200 + correct content-type; blob missing → 200 placeholder (+ warning for badge / flag); backend error → 503. * [ ] The `/api/footy/.+/(?:mugshot|badge|flag)$` entry is removed from `linkinator.config.json` and the SYS-572 README note updated, so the link-check job exercises these endpoints again (against an instance where storage is reachable). * [ ] `typecheck` / `lint` / `format:check` / `knip` and unit coverage all green. ## Related * **SYS-572** — Add broken link checking to CI pipeline (surfaced this; currently skips these endpoints).

fields.description: ## Problem The three Azure-blob-backed image routes throw and return HTTP 500 whenever blob storage is unavailable or misconfigured, and their "specific blob missing" behaviour is inconsistent: | Route | Blob missing (backend healthy) | Backend unavailable | Unknown entity | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `GET /api/footy/player/[id]/mugshot` | falls back to `manofmystery.jpg` in the same container — but 500s if _that_ is missing | 500 | `null` → 404 only for a NaN id or a player row that doesn't exist | | `GET /api/footy/club/[id]/badge` | `null` → 404 | 500 | no entity check — a bad id is indistinguishable from a missing blob (both 404) | | `GET /api/footy/country/[fifaCode]/flag` | `null` → 404 | 500 | no entity check | Consequences on the live site: * Every `` pointing at one of these (player lists, game pages, `FamilyTree`, `PlayerCountryMap`, `DrinkersForm`, `MoneyForm`, `UserButton`, `GameInvitationResponseForm`, …) shows a broken image on any transient Azure blip, and each request logs an error-level event via `captureUnexpectedError` in `handleGET`. * SYS-572's link-check crawl of a full-data instance reported **1442 broken links, every one of them** `/api/footy/player/{id}/mugshot` → 500, because PR CI has no storage credentials (by design — PR workflows never touch 1Password). The endpoints are currently excluded in `linkinator.config.json` via `/api/footy/.+/(?:mugshot|badge|flag)$` pending this fix. ## Decision — split the three failure modes 1. **Unknown / invalid entity** (non-numeric id, no player / club / country row) → **404**. Add the missing entity-existence checks to the badge and flag routes so "no such club" is distinguishable from "club exists, badge blob missing". 2. **Storage backend unavailable** (missing creds, network error, Azure 5xx / timeout) → **503** + error-level capture. Same for all three: nothing can be served and it must be loud. 3. **Specific blob missing, backend healthy** — differs by resource contract: * **Mugshot** (`blob-or-default` contract; most players have no photo): serve the fallback placeholder, **200**, no alert (debug log only). * **Badge / flag** (`blob-always` contract; every valid club / country ought to have one): serve a generic placeholder, **200**, **warning-level alert** naming the club id / FIFA code, so the missing data gets fixed without breaking the page or spamming error-level events. Ship a bundled last-resort placeholder **inside the app** (e.g. `src/assets/…`) for each resource so the response never depends on a second blob fetch succeeding. `manofmystery.jpg` in the mugshots container stays the preferred mugshot fallback; the bundled asset is the final resort when even that can't be fetched. Factor the shared path into one helper, e.g. `fetchBlobOrFallback(container, key, { fallbackKey?, bundledFallback, onFallback })`, with each route supplying its own entity check and `onFallback` (silent for mugshot, `log.warn` for badge / flag). ## Acceptance criteria * \[ \] `GET /api/footy/club/[id]/badge` and `.../country/[fifaCode]/flag` return 404 for an unknown club / country, distinct from a missing blob. * \[ \] All three routes return a 200 image (real or placeholder) whenever the entity is valid and the storage backend is reachable — including when the specific blob is absent. * \[ \] Storage-backend failure returns **503** (not 500) and is captured at error level. * \[ \] A missing badge / flag blob for a valid entity emits a warning-level event identifying the entity; a missing mugshot blob does not. * \[ \] A bundled in-repo placeholder exists for each resource and is served when no blob (including the container-level fallback) is available. * \[ \] Route unit tests cover: unknown entity → 404; blob present → 200 + correct content-type; blob missing → 200 placeholder (+ warning for badge / flag); backend error → 503. * \[ \] The `/api/footy/.+/(?:mugshot|badge|flag)$` entry is removed from `linkinator.config.json` and the SYS-572 README note updated, so the link-check job exercises these endpoints again (against an instance where storage is reachable). * \[ \] `typecheck` / `lint` / `format:check` / `knip` and unit coverage all green. ## Related * **SYS-572** — Add broken link checking to CI pipeline (surfaced this; currently skips these endpoints).

file.content:
## Broken Link Checking

[`.github/workflows/link-check.yml`](.github/workflows/link-check.yml) builds the app, runs it against the seeded CI database, and uses [`linkinator`](https://github.com/JustinBeckwith/linkinator) to recursively crawl the **public** surface from `http://127.0.0.1:3000`. Any non-skipped internal link that returns a 4xx/5xx fails the workflow (and therefore the PR check). The full JSON report is uploaded as a build artifact on every run.

External hosts are deliberately out of scope here so PRs don't break on third-party outages — those are covered by the separate weekly external-link job (SYS-616).

Exclusions live in [`linkinator.config.json`](linkinator.config.json) at the repo root: add a per-URL or per-domain regular expression to the `skip` array to stop a link being checked. The first entry (`^https?://(?!127\.0\.0\.1:3000)`) is what scopes the crawl to internal links; leave it in place and add new exclusions alongside it. The authenticated `src/app/footy/**` admin surface is not yet crawled (it needs the mock-auth cookie and the programmatic API — a follow-up).

To run it locally, start a production build on port 3000 and point the script at it:

```shell
op run --env-file ./.env -- npm run build
npm run start:ci &
npm run linkcheck
```

Make sure nothing else is already bound to port 3000 first (a stray `next dev`, or VS Code's Live Preview) — `npm run linkcheck` just crawls whatever answers on `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, and a static file server there will happily serve the whole working tree.

## Sentry Sampling and Quota Controls

The Sentry setup in this project now uses conservative defaults designed to fit
